description: Our project focuses on finding places on Earth that share similar environmental and geological features with the Moon and Mars. By exploring NASA datasets, satellite imagery, and scientific research, we aim to identify and characterize new analogue locations that could help prepare for future lunar and Martian missions.
summary: 'Analog Atlas' is an interactive geospatial platform designed to identify and evaluate terrestrial environments suitable for practical testing and research in preparation for lunar and Martian exploration. Using a mission-driven approach, it examines proposed planetary projects and their specific requirements to establish purpose-specific evaluation metrics and identify relevant Earth-based analogs. Each selected location is assessed through two indicators: the Similarity Index (SI) and Exploration Capability (EC). By combining scientific data, evidence-based evaluations, and interactive mapping, Analog Atlas helps researchers discover specialized terrestrial testing environments and make more informed decisions when preparing for future planetary missions.
details:
Introduction

'Analog Atlas' is an interactive geospatial platform designed to identify, evaluate, and visualize terrestrial environments that serve as analogs for specific locations and environmental conditions on the Moon and Mars.

Rather than prioritizing environmental similarity, 'Analog Atlas' categorizes them according to their potential applications in planetary exploration, such as rover testing, human habitat research, astrobiology, and geological investigations.

Methodology

Our methodology began with reviewing scientific research papers and proposed lunar and Martian projects to identify their specific scientific objectives, technological requirements, and environmental needs. Based on these findings, we established purpose-specific evaluation metrics and identified terrestrial locations that could serve as practical testing environments, prioritizing sites that strongly represented particular characteristics relevant to specific mission objectives rather than requiring complete environmental resemblance. We then compiled relevant geological, environmental, and geographical data for each selected analog and developed two evaluation indicators: the Similarity Index (SI), measuring scientific resemblance, and Exploration Capability (EC), assessing relevance to practical exploration requirements. Finally, we organized the collected data, metrics, evidence, and evaluations into an interactive geospatial platform, developed with assistance from Claude.

Platform Features

Analog Overview

This page contains an overall report on all findings, along with easy navigation to other features. Interactive elements were used for a user-friendly experience exploring and understanding dense analog data. The search bar allows users to be specific with their categorization and choose the analog fitted for their needs.

The map includes all analog sites. Upon toggling over a single site, a user can gain direct access to it’s dossier and a short overview. Mars and Moon targets are indicated through separate colors.

This shows the metrics used to denote each ‘Purpose Group’, along with their mean Similarity Index (SI).

The candidate index is used to present all the candidates and their scores in one view.

Purpose Groups

Each ‘Purpose Group’ is presented through two tabs:  ‘Metrics & Scoring’ and ‘Analogs’. ‘Metrics and Scoring’ includes the used metrics, scientific parameters, Similarity Index (SI) and Environmental Correspondence (EC) equations, and variable introduction. Sliders are implemented to provide a better understanding of SI for users. ['Robotic Mobility & Terrain Operations' used as an example]

Note: SI and EC are based on the predetermined metrics; therefore, the scores can contain errors due to the lack of classification needed.

The ‘Analog’ tab lists all the analog sites in the ‘Purpose Group’ and provides access to each analog page.

Analog Page

The ‘Analog’ tabs lists all the analog sites in the ‘Purpose Group’ and an access to each analog page.

Each analog page starts with an analog site and target site introduction along with its SI and EC scores. [‘Qaidam Basin, China’ used as example].

A sliding morphological comparison is used to show visual similarity between two sites

‘Measured Characteristics’ include data comparison between two sites according to the pre-determined metrics. It provides supporting geological, environmental, and scientific evidence explaining why a particular location qualifies as an analog.

Field evidence helps with mission suitability correspondence, and 'Terrestrial Mismatches' highlights environmental differences and limitations.

Lastly, publications and datasets used to compile this analog are stated.

References

Provides relevant scientific resources and datasets to support comparative data and analysis.

Further Implementation & Studies

More Earth sites, metrics, and 'Purpose Groups' could be explored.

Conclusion

Analog Atlas was created to bridge the gap between planetary exploration research and practical field testing. By connecting proposed lunar and Martian mission requirements with carefully selected terrestrial environments, we aim to make the search for relevant testing grounds more systematic, accessible, and scientifically informed. Rather than simply identifying places that resemble extraterrestrial landscapes, our platform helps researchers discover locations suited to specific exploration objectives, supporting better preparation for future missions. Ultimately, we believe that understanding other worlds begins with making better use of our own.

Analog Atlas — From Testing Grounds to Frontier.
